memory_candidates.content: When a bash script spawns several separate python3 heredocs (one per function), the biggest duplicate-block finding is often not repeated HELPER functions but an entire duplicate PIPELINE: a function that re-runs its whole search/computation a second time (e.g. 'retry without a filter if the filtered attempt returned zero rows') as a second, separately-interpolated heredoc. Extracting shared helpers into one file-local python module (imported via sys.path.insert from each heredoc) fixes the helper duplication, but the bigger win is restructuring the caller to invoke the now-shared pipeline function TWICE IN-PROCESS instead of running two heredocs -- this eliminates the second python3 invocation entirely rather than merely deduplicating what it contained. Roughly half of a -363 NET-PROD figure came from this restructuring, not from the helper-function move alone.

When writing a characterization test for a script with has_test:false before a self-internal-duplication refactor (peers=0 in script-inventory.sh), capture every tested mode's raw stdout+exit code to files under a caller-overridable CAPTURE_DIR directory, then run the SAME test script once against the unmodified code and once against the refactored code, and diff -r the two capture directories. This reuses one test file as both the pass/fail oracle and the before/after byte-identical-output oracle, and works cleanly as long as no absolute temp path (mktemp dir, git toplevel) leaks into any captured JSON output -- verify that by construction (pop/never-emit any internal path field) rather than by normalizing paths after the fact.

Bash 5.3's `local` builtin, under `set -u`, treats every name declared in a single multi-assignment `local` statement as unset until the WHOLE statement finishes -- so `local a="$1" b="$a"` raises 'a: unbound variable' even though `a` was assigned earlier in the same statement. This is a real behavior (reproduced minimally), not a one-off typo. Fix: split into separate `local` statements (`local a="$1"` then `local b="$a"`) whenever a later name in the list needs to read an earlier one.
